title: Conor Benn to fight American Regis Prograis in first bout with Zuffa Boxing
content:
Conor Benn’s first fight since signing with Zuffa Boxing will be against American Regis Prograis on April 11, as the co-main event to Tyson Fury’s comeback fight against Arslanbek Makhmudov at the Tottenham Hotspur stadium.

Benn’s switch from Matchroom, the Eddie Hearn-led company that has promoted him from the start of his professional career a decade ago, to the promotional company formed by Saudi Arabia-backed sports events company Sela and U.S. combat sports giants TKO Group Holdings, and fronted by UFC CEO Dana White, was announced last Friday.

It has since been confirmed, by TKO president and CEO Mark Shapiro, that the deal linking the 29-year-old Brit to Zuffa is currently for one fight only. Speaking on a quarterly financial call this Wednesday Shapiro said, “Of course, we hope eventually he’ll fight in our Zuffa Boxing series, exclusively on Paramount+, but for now, this is just one fight.”

He added that Benn’s reported purse of $15million is being covered not by TKO but by Sela, just as was the case with Terence Crawford’s fight against Saul ‘Canelo’ Alvarez last September.

Benn (24-1, 14 KOs), will take on Prograis (30-3, 24 KOs) at the same stadium where he fought Chris Eubank Jr last time out in November 2025, in a middleweight contest that Benn won convincingly. This time, he’s taking on a 37-year-old former super lightweight world champion, at a weight likely to be higher than the 140lbs Prograis is accustomed to fighting at. Benn is a natural welterweight at 147lbs, though he has not boxed at that weight since 2022.

In a release announcing the fight, which will be broadcast by streaming platform Netflix, Benn said: “April 11th can’t come soon enough, returning to Tottenham Hotspur Stadium again, where I made history against Eubank Jr means everything to me. My last fight there showed the world exactly who I am and what I’m about. Fighting on the biggest stages, in the biggest shows, I fear no one!”

Prograis said: “Last time I fought in London, Conor Benn was on my undercard, so this is a full-circle moment for me. But this circle will close with me teaching him a lesson on April 11th. He’s not fighting some weight-drained super middleweight. I am in shape and will bring home this victory.”
